Fire Weather Planning Forecast for Western and Central North Dakota
National Weather Service Bismarck ND
202 PM CDT Thu Oct 22 2026

.DISCUSSION...

Clear and calm weather is found across western and central North 
Dakota today. Highs are broadly in the 70s, with minimum relative 
humidity dropping as low as 35 percent over portions of the far 
southwest. Light south to southeast winds sustained around 10 to 
15 MPH and gusting as high as 20 MPH are expected through the 
early evening. Low temperatures tonight drop to the mid 40s 
northwest to the mid 50s south central, with max humidity recover 
only as low as 95 percent. 

For Friday, partly to mostly cloudy skies are expected across the
forecast area. Highs are forecast from the lower 70s to lower 
80s, with minimum relative humidity dropping as low as 20 to 25 
percent in the far southwest. With gusty southwest winds sustained
around 20 to 25 MPH and gusting as high as 35 MPH in the far 
southwest in the afternoon, near critical fire weather conditions 
are expected. 

The passage of a cold front Friday evening through Saturday 
morning is expected to strengthen winds and turn them out of the 
west, with sustained speeds up to 30 to 35 MPH and gusts up to 45 
MPH overnight. Winds will somewhat diminish Saturday afternoon, 
though will remain breezy through early Saturday evening. Cooler 
high temperatures are expected Saturday afternoon, forecast from 
the mid 40s to mid 50s. Minimum relative humidity is expected to 
drop as low as 25 in the far southwest, though more broadly 
greater than 30 percent elsewhere. Thus, critical fire weather 
conditions are not currently expected on Saturday. Cooler weather 
is expected persist through the weekend into next week.
